## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Todeyyamāṇavapucchā* ("The Questions of the Student Todeyya") is the tenth discourse of the *Pārāyaṇavagga*, the fifth chapter of the *Suttanipāta* in the Khuddaka Nikāya, beginning at verse 1088 [Hazra 1994; Norman 1997-2001; Saddhatissa 2013]. The sutta concerns how to recognize an emancipated person. In response to the student Todeyya, the Buddha explains that no further deliverance exists for one who is freed from lust, craving, and doubt, and who has attained true understanding and fully realized the Dhamma [Hazra 1994].

In the canonical exegetical tradition, the discourse is commented upon in the *Todeyyamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 13) and referenced in the *Pucchā* (Cnd 2) of the *Cūḷaniddesa*.
